expectations.text: Flags that transfer()'s fromAccount and toAccount are both plain strings and can be swapped silently
expectations.evidence: No mention of the two account parameters being interchangeable strings or of branded/nominal IDs; the transfer() findings cover only the missing transaction (#1) and non-null assertions (#7).

expectations.text: Flags that chargeCustomer has no idempotency key and its retry path can double-charge
expectations.evidence: Idempotency is raised only for the webhook: 'No idempotency in webhook handler (lines 93-100) ... Stripe retries webhooks.' chargeCustomer's own retry path / missing idempotency key is never flagged.

expectations.text: Flags the catch block that returns null as swallowing the error
expectations.evidence: 'Silent charge failures — chargeCustomer() returns null (line 59) Failed charges return null instead of throwing. Callers that don't explicitly check for null will think the charge succeeded.'

expectations.text: Flags money being held as a JS number (float) rather than integer minor units
expectations.evidence: 'Floating-point money — applyDiscount() ... produces values like 19.999999999999996. Use integer cents throughout, or a decimal library.'

expectations.text: Flags the interpolated raw SQL in purgeCanceledAccounts
expectations.evidence: 'SQL injection — purgeCanceledAccounts() (line 87) ... Direct string interpolation into raw SQL.'

expectations.text: Flags the non-exhaustive switch over subscription status
expectations.evidence: 'Switch without default case — updateSubscription() (lines 70-77) Statuses like "paused", "past_due", "trialing" fall through silently.'

expectations.text: Flags JSON.parse of the webhook body as unvalidated external input
expectations.evidence: Only signature verification is raised ('Without stripe.webhooks.constructEvent() verification'); no mention of JSON.parse or the parsed payload's shape being trusted/unvalidated.

expectations.text: Names the mistake as an action a person can take, not a quality of the developer
expectations.evidence: Findings are stated as code conditions and actions — 'These two operations need to be wrapped in a database transaction', 'Use integer cents throughout' — with no characterization of the developer.

expectations.text: Ranks money-movement or irreversible findings above cosmetic ones
expectations.evidence: Critical section leads with 'Money can vanish — transfer() has no transaction' and 'Double-charging customers'; 'Unused variable' is last under Medium.

expectations.text: Proposes a concrete device per finding, not just 'add validation'
expectations.evidence: Several findings carry no device: #2 SQL injection has no parameterized-query fix, #3 double-charge, #7 non-null assertions, #10 missing default case, and #11 unused variable state the problem only ('Dead code or forgotten implementation?').

expectations.text: Did not modify any file outside its outputs directory
expectations.evidence: Response is analysis only, ending with an offer — 'Want me to draft fixes for any of these?' — no edits reported.
